If you want to get back into weight training, restart with a solid beginner's program based on compound lifts like SL 5x5 or Starting Strength. I don't know how tolerated the Fittit attitude is around here (just got here), but squats>anything.

Just to add to what everyone else has said, there is a difference between how to train for strength or aesthetics. I was in almost the same boat as you about half a year ago. That being said, like many people have stated a good beginner 5x5 will pack on strength and volume quickly if you haven't trained in a while.

The rule of thumb for a lot of weight lifters is around 3-5 rep sets for power, 6-8 for strength, and 9-14 for volume. This is a generalization used for most core lifts like bench and squat. As a rule of thumb don't train your biceps using a 5x5 workout or other auxiliaries.

The quickest way to get your cardio in shape is with a sprint interval program 2 to 3 days a week. Look it up, it's highly effective. Avoid injuries by properly warming up and correcting your form in front of a mirror. Find some good YouTube videos if you aren't absolutely sure about your form on a particular exercise.

The current limits are a very bad idea. Extending them is even worse.

Why?

Any community that has restrictions on members that are not popular has a tendency to devolve into a toxic community of cliques and power users. It happened to Stack Exchange. It happened to Hacker News. And it will happen here if things don't change.

Think of what restrictions on new users cause people who are new to the site to think.

It ends up doing two things. First, it drives away a lot of people. This is generally a bad thing, although I acknowledge that it isn't always.

However, the second thing is the problem. Namely, it ends up with people posting things solely for the sake of getting points. Not for the sake of other people, or for the sake of sharing interesting things, or for the sake of, well, anything good, really.

And it also actively discourages people from posting interesting discussions. It is far easier to get points by ~~~posting~~~ spamming low-effort comments everywhere then by actually posting things that spark discussion. Because the more interesting discussion you could have about something, the more likely it is that people will disagree with you.

And especially when there are limits to downvotes. As most people with downvotes will end up restricting them to worse things than simply low-effort comments, as otherwise they will run out.

For cliques to exist the limit would have to be way, way higher at ~2000 ccp. The current limit is extremely low and can be obtained in hours and days at most.

As for people leaving I already spoke about this in another comment here:

https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/119366/254518

The very existence of a limit is enough.

Look at what happens to someone who just entered the site. They browse a while, eventually decide to make an account. They upvote a few things. And then they hit a wall. And now, here's where the problem happens.

You see, ultimately there are three types of users.

Some users will hit the wall, and bounce. Just leave.

Some users will think "meh", and just roll with it.

But some users will see it as a challenge, and start posting things for the sake of becoming popular.

Any wall will cause this.

And unfortunately, you seem relatively set on thinking this is not a problem. Meh. It will become a problem, sooner or later, and when it does I'm out of here.

I just wish that the spiral could be avoided in the first place.
